title: MariaDB save intermittently fails with safe-update-mode error while moving connections
author: n3cr0cr0w
body_snippet:
## Description

When using the MariaDB backend, saving the connection list intermittently fails if MariaDB/MySQL safe-update mode is enabled.

The failure is not consistent. While moving connections around in the connection tree, approximately 50% of save attempts produced the safe-update error. Other save attempts completed successfully. When a save succeeds, the entire connection tree is saved.

comments.author: n3cr0cr0w
comments.snippet: Yes, last couple of releases have been working much better. Sometimes it still fails to update tblRoot (I just rename it for testing). No errors and it doesn't break my workflow.

comments.author: robertpopa22
n3cr0cr0w
comments.snippet: It is saving tblRoot on change, no errors/warning. I verified the change was saved after closing. On open it is re-loading as 'New Folder (xxx)' no matter what is saved in the DB... Strange that it is correct in the DB.

comments.author: n3cr0cr0w
comments.snippet:
After making a connection, the tblRoot is updated to 'New Folder (xxx)' with a ConfVersion of 3.2

Not sure if this is helpful, when it saves the rename the ConfVersion is updated to 3.5.

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Both of your observations were precise hits, and each was its own bug. Thank you for including the ConfVersion numbers — they turned this from a mystery into an arrest.

**1. ConfVersion flapping 3.5 → 3.2 (`3f13a6e56`).** Every SQL save was stamping `tblRoot.ConfVersion` from a stale constant that belongs to the *XML file format* — frozen at 3.2 — while the SQL schema is at 3.5.
